 ::J U D G M E N T:
:
The petitioner has filed this claim petition against the respondents U/Sec.166 of M.V.
Act seeking compensation for the damages caused to his car in the road traffic accident took place on 16.04.2024.
2. Brief case of the petitioner in the nutshell:

It is the case of the petitioner that on 16.04.2024 at about 9.05 p.m, the petitioner and his son were returning from Kunigal in his Maruti Vitara Breeza car bearing Reg.No.KA- SCCH-23 04-MW-0804, when they reached near Bhadrapura Gate, Bengaluru - Hassan high way NH-75 road, (Opposite to Suzuku Showroom) by following all the traffic rules and regulations, at that time the respondent No.1 who is the owner and driver of the Maruti Vitara Breeza car bearing Reg.No.KA-52-N-0518 driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner without following any traffic rules and regulations, so as to endanger human life and dashed against to the rear side of the petitioner's car.
Due to impact the petitioner's car had hit the barricade which was on the left side of the Highway.
In view of the accident, both back side and front side of the petitioner's car damaged extensively as detailed in IMV Report.
After IMV inspection the petitioner was shifted his damaged car for repair.
The service center has issued estimation of Rs.4,44,116.72 on 24.04.2024.
Till today the car of the petitioner is in the authorized service centre only.

He alleged that he has paid a sum of Rs.25,000/- on SCCH-23 09.05.2024 and another a sum of Rs.25,000/-
on 10.05.2024 by way of cash towards the repair of the car.
It is alleged that from the date of accident, the petitioner car was lying in the service centre, only and the petitioner was not having any other car for him to commute along with his family.

The petitioner was constrained to hire a private taxi to commute to his native and also other places as and when required to travel along with his family and a sum of Rs.50,000/- expenses has incurred in this regard thereby he undergoing great mental shock and huge pecuniary loss.
It is further urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-52-N-0518.
The respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
SCCH-23 3.
Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.

sentences.text: After service of notice, respondent No.2 appeared before the Court by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Maruti Vitara Breeza car bearing Reg.No.KA- 52-N-0518.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
This respondent denied negligence on the part of the driver of its insured vehicle.
Per contra it is contended that as the accident has taken place due to the negligence of driver of petitioner's car.
This petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured car did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
SCCH-23
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further contended that the petitioner has reimbursed the amount from his insurer for the damages of the above vehicle from the accident with consent, it is full and final settlement.
Again claiming the same is bad in law.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that his Maruthi Vitara Breeza car bearing reg.No.KA-04-MW- 0804 sustained damages in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 16.04.2024 at about 9.05 p.m,
near Bhadrapura Gate (Yazaki Showroom), on Bengaluru - Hassan NH-75 Highway road, Solur Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagara District, due to the actionable negligence of the driver of another Breeza car bearing reg.No.KA-52-N-0518 ?
SCCH-23 2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, to what extent and from whom ?
3
. What order and award?
6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's. P1 to 21 were marked on his behalf.
The respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence on its behalf.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.2 counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-

3 Issue No.1 - In the Affirmative Issue No.2 - In the Negative Issue No.3 - As per final order for the following:
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1: PW.1-Sri Rangadhamaiah.

sentences.text: R.S filed his affidavit reiterating the petition averments.
In support of his case he has produced the following documents as SCCH-23 per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.21.

The evidence of PW.1 is fortified by the above documents, which clearly show that based on the FIR lodged by the petitioner himself, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed Charge sheet against the driver of offending Maruti Vitara Breeza car bearing Reg.No.KA-52-N-0518 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC.
Ex.P.10 - IMV Report discloses that the petitioner's vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-0804 was damaged in the accident.
PW.1 was cross examined at length by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
But nothing worthwhile was elicited from his mouth to discredit his testimony.
The Insurance Company has not made any attempt to examine the driver of the offending Car to show that there was no negligence on his part in causing the accident.
Moreover the police documents are not disputed by the respondent No.2.

Under these circumstances the evidence of PW.1 coupled with SCCH-23 documentary evidence establishes that the accident in question occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Maruti Vitara Breeza car bearing Reg.No.KA-52-N-0518.
With this observation Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

10. ISSUE NO.2: Service Estimation, 2- receipts, amount paid receipts (3 no's), Assessment sheet cum settlement summary (6 pages), Tax invoice (10 page), Tax invoice (6 page) are exhibited by the petitioner at Ex.P.12 to 17.

In the course of his cross-examination, PW.1 admitted the following facts:
    .   , 
,       . ..15                
 .
SCCH-23

As per the admission of petitioner, the said exhibits manifestly make it clear that the petitioner has received the repair charges for the damage sustained by his car in a Road Traffic Accident from his own insurer.

Admittedly the insurer of the petitioner's vehicle would have paid such amount only after conducting survey i.e, on the basis of survey report and after deducting of depreciation etc., Hence such amount would obviously be paid towards full and final settlement.

11. The elicitation supra disclose that the petitioner has already claimed the compensation towards damage sustained by his car and the same is settled by his personal Insurance Company towards full and final settlement.
The said aspect of full and final settlement of the O.D. Claim of the petitioner by his insurer is not challenged by him before any authority except filing this petition.
If he was not satisfied with the amount paid SCCH-23 under his O.D. Claim, he should have challenged the said settlement stating that it falls short of his actual claim.
However for the best reasons known to him the petitioner has not chosen to do so.

Neither has he produced any letter or endorsement issued by his insurer to show that liberty was given to him to receive the remaining amount relating to repairs of his car from the Insurance Company of the offending car.

sentences.text:
In the light of above said facts and circumstances reliance is placed upon a decision reported in 2005 ACJ 1332 between Harkhu Bai and others V/s Jiyaram and others, wherein Hon'ble Apex Court held that: "Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, section 166- Claim application- Damage to property- Estoppel-Truck 'B' was damaged in accident due to negligence of driver of truck 'A- Owner of truck 'B' received compensation in full and final settlement of his claim from his Insurance SCCH-23 Company- Whether the owner of truck 'B' can claim compensation from Insurance Company of truck 'A'- Held:
No."

entities.text: Harkhu Bai and others V/s Jiyaram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Likewise in the present case also the petitioner has received the compensation towards the damage caused to his vehicle from his Insurance Company under OD claim in full and final settlement without any reservation or demur.
The damage was assessed and paid after receipt of survey report and estimation from the service center where petitioner's vehicle was repaired.
Hence he is estopped from claiming any further compensation from the insurer of offending car.

13. In this regard respondent is also relied on the decision reported in ILR 2010 KAR 3962 between New India Assurance Company Ltd., Belgaum Divisional Office through its Regional Officer V/s M/s Sharmila Devdas and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that once full and final settlement is SCCH-23 received the claimant is deprived of claiming again.
Considering these aspects the respondents are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
In fact the claim itself is not sustainable.

In the absence of any materials to show that claim paid by the Insurance Company, with which the petitioner's vehicle was insured represented only a part of the total damages, it is not safe to rely only on mere pleadings and oral evidence of the petitioner to grant compensation.
Therefore in the considered view of this Tribunal, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered in the Negative.
14. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of discussion made supra, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed U/s.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby dismissed.
SCCH-23 No order as to cost.
Draw award accordingly.
